episodes.177242: A strong upper trough moved across the region on March 21 and 22. This system produced strong winds across the West Side Hills, the Sierra Nevada and across the Kern County Mountains and Deserts where several stations measured gusts exceeding 60 mph. In addition, heavy snow fell in the Sierra Nevada where several high elevation SNOTEL stations picked up between 18 and 30 inches of new snow while liquid precipitation totals were generally between 1 and 2 inches. Much of the San Joaquin Valley picked up between a quarter and three quarters of an inch of additional rainfall over an already saturated ground while thunderstorm outflow winds knocked down several trees in and around Fresno during the afternoon of March 21.
episodes.178634: Another cold upper level system led to widespread precipitation and strong winds in Southern California on March 21st through the 23rd.
episodes.178636: Warm and wet system brought periods of heavy rain with flooding. Snow levels were high, with 1 to 2 feet of snow accumulating above 6,500 feet, locally more on higher peaks. Heavy rain on already saturated areas fell bringing additional roadway flooding, as well as local mudslides. Evacuations were ordered in San Joaquin County due to flooding. Thunderstorms with large hail, strong damaging winds and funnel clouds were reported. Strong winds gusting to 40 to 58 mph brought down trees and powerlines across the area, causing power outages.
episodes.178982: Strong low pressure moving into the West Coast brought rain and isolated severe thunderstorms to the Mojave Desert, as well as heavy snow to the Spring Mountains.
episodes.179034: The first in a series of disturbances moved across Arizona from March 20 to 21. This caused widespread snow showers to develop.  The heaviest snow was over the higher terrain in upslope areas. This storm also delivered strong and damaging winds. The higher snow levels caused significant melting of lower elevation snow and flooding. The flooding took several days to flow down major rivers in northern Arizona.

events.location: 9.76 WNW Las Vegas N Air Term
events.narrative: Rain throughout the Las Vegas Valley led to multiple crashes on the freeways. One man was killed when his vehicle overturned while traveling too fast for the wet conditions.
De Luz Road was closed due to flooding. About 0.50-0.70 inch of rain fell in this area in the 12hrs prior.
In the Rainbow area, Huffstatler St was closed from 5th St to 2nd St due to flooding. About 0.50-0.70 inch of rain fell in the 12 hours prior.
In Escondido, Country Club Drive was closed south of Harmony Grove Road due to flooding.
Flooding was reported in Lane 2 at the intersection of SR75 and Attu Avenue. Rainfall of 0.60 inch fell in the previous 6 hours.
The I-8 East on ramp at Texas Street was flooded, with water up to vehicle tires. Rainfall of 0.70 to 0.80 inches fell in the previous 6 hours.
Flooding on Vesper Road lead to multiple vehicle spinouts. About 0.90 to 1.10 inches of rain fell in this area in the previous 12 hours.

Tonto Creek near Roosevelt started to rise from a level of 3.7 feet (630 CFS) at around 1100 AM on March 21.  The flooding started earlier upstream. The first peak flow of 12.2 feet (23,300 CFS) was at 800 PM on March 21. A second peak of 12.5 feet (25,500 CFS) was observed at 800 AM on March 22. The gauge dropped back down to action level at (4.35 feet) on March 25 at 800 AM. An elderly couple and their dog were killed in the Bear Flat area when they cross the flooded Tonto Creek in their truck.
The off-ramp on I-5 North at La Jolla Village Drive was flooded. About 0.65 inch of rain fell in the previous 6 hours.

The stream gauge on Oak Creek in Sedona rose above action stage at  (7 feet) at 900 AM on March 21.  It reached a peak of 16.35 feet at 600 AM on March 22 and then dropped below 7 feet around 1100 PM March 22.  Flood stage is at 14.0 feet.
In Murrieta, the parking lot in front of the local Sam's Club was flooded with water about 1 foot deep.
A large tree was downed near Weidners Garden.

A swiftwater rescue was needed near Cajon Boulevard and Swarthout Canyon Road after a vehicle tried to cross high water and got swept away in the current. The vehicle was swept approximately 100 yards down the river and was not recoverable.

Roads near the intersection of Anza Road and De Portola Road were shut down due to flowing water and a mud slide. A jeep vehicle required a rescue after it was stuck in 2 feet of flowing water and mud. About 1.4 inches of rain fell in this area in the previous 12 hours, with 1 inch falling in 6 hours.
A large tree was downed, resulting in a power outage.

The USGS stream gage at Wet Beaver Creek two crests. The first one was from 1000 AM to 400 PM on March 21 and the second one was from 700 AM to 1200 PM on March 22.  Clogging of the gauge affected the actual flows.  Media showed pictures and videos of property and homes flooded in Rimrock along East Beaver Vista and East Sycamore Lanes (both on 3/21 and 3/22).
The eastbound right-hand lane of Murrieta Hot Springs Road was flooded by a 3-foot waterfall from Warm Springs Creek. About 1.4 inches of rain fell in this area in the previous 12 hours.

The river gauge on the Little Colorado River near Cameron showed a spike starting around 1100 AM on March 21.  The river dropped back down and then showed a steady increase again around noon on March 23 corresponding to flows arriving from the Winslow area. The river at Cameron dropped back down again by the evening of March 25.  The hydrograph on the LCR at the Colorado River showed the same trace 6 hours later...dropping down around noon on March 26.
Several reported trees and power lines were downed in Fresno during the early afternoon of March 21.
Low-lying portions of Barona Road and Wildcat Canyon Road were flooded. Total rainfall of 1.6 inches occurred.
About 2 inches of rain fell at Palomar Mountain nearby, leading to the San Luis Rey River flowing over Cole Grade Road with water 1 to 2 feet deep.
A trained spotter reported fast-moving water over Via Montezuma at Murrieta Creek, prompting a road closure.
A trained spotter in Temecula shared a photo of a flooded road crossing near Murrieta Creek.
Spotter SO-47 reported rotation in a funnel cloud near Leisure Town Road and Alamo Drive.
Strong straight-line winds downed multiple trees and utility poles near downtown Woodland. Sacramento International Airport reported a max gust of 46 mph. Time was estimated by radar.
